In [[mathematics]], an '''invariant polynomial''' is a [[polynomial]] <math>P</math> that is [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] under a [[group (mathematics)|group]] <math>\Gamma</math> [[Group action (mathematics)|acting]] on a [[vector space]] <math>V</math>. Therefore, <math>P</math> is a <math>\Gamma</math>-invariant polynomial if

:<math>P(\gamma x) = P(x)</math>

for all <math>\gamma \in \Gamma</math> and <math>x \in V</math>.<ref>{{cite web|title=invariant polynomial in nLab|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/invariant+polynomial|website=ncatlab.org}}</ref>

Cases of particular importance are for &Gamma; a [[finite group]] (in the theory of [[Molien series]], in particular), a [[compact group]], a [[Lie group]] or [[algebraic group]]. For a basis-independent definition of 'polynomial' nothing is lost by referring to the [[symmetric power]]s of the given [[linear representation]] of &Gamma;.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Draisma|first1=Jan|last2=Gijswijt|first2=Dion|title=Invariant Theory with Applications|url=http://www.win.tue.nl/~jdraisma/teaching/invtheory0910/lecturenotes11.pdf}}</ref>
